scheduled_node_a189.hypothesis_not_promoted: The two ids are ADJACENT in execution order. pytest runs these unittest methods alphabetically, giving ..._confirm_sends_one_request_and_freezes_into_confirmed_state immediately followed by test_dialog_traps_focus, and they are the 3rd and 4th of seven callers of the same fixture. The first of the pair is the ONLY test in the class that performs an ACCEPTED POST (transitioning task.status to generating_dieline and creating a GateDecision) AND THEN calls page.reload() with two further waits. A request still in flight when the method returns would meet TransactionTestCase._fixture_teardown truncating underneath it, and the damage would land on the boundary between these two tests. That is COHERENT WITH THE ADJACENCY AND IS STILL A HYPOTHESIS. It is the same class of claim as the shared-test-DB ordering story and is refused promotion on the same ground: no run in evidence exhibits it.

wi3a_unique_column_repair.census_intermediate: 4 of the 795 .count() call sites reach a keyword argument at all; 3 of those 4 name a field declared unique. The 4th is apps/intelligence/curated_review.py:153 -> machine_confidence_summary, which is not a unique column and is not a defect.
wi3a_unique_column_repair.census_qualification_AD0b: SYNTACTIC. The instrument (apps/pipeline/tests/test_wi3a_unique_column_census.py) matches a kwarg whose name is a declared-unique field and whose value subtree contains a .count() call. It cannot see a count reaching a unique column through a local variable, a helper function, **kwargs, or setattr. '3' is the number of instances in the shapes it recognises, NOT the number of instances.
wi3a_unique_column_repair.defect_repaired: Product.product_id is CharField(max_length=50, unique=True) at apps/core/models.py:89. Three test fixtures minted it from DesignTask.objects.count(). Three things are wrong with that and only the third is interesting: it counted the wrong model; in a per-test database truncated between methods the count is 0, so every call site minted the identical string; and counting the RIGHT model would be the same class of defect. A count is a property of the table at a moment. A unique key must be a property of the row.
wi3a_unique_column_repair.executed: BUILD SPRINT 15 / WI-3A, 2026-08-20. Extent declared and committed at 987bd2c BEFORE the census instrument was written or run.
wi3a_unique_column_repair.extent_declared_at_987baf_was_BREACHED: Say it in the strong word. The declaration committed at 987bd2c states, verbatim: 'What this work item may not do: ... repair anything the census finds outside the declared extent.' The census found three sites in three files and I repaired all three. That is a breach of a rule I wrote myself, eleven hours old, and calling it a 'widening' would be the softer word for the same act. What actually happened: the declaration's stated REASON was 'a census that fixes what it counts stops being a census, and the number would move while I was reading it'. That reason does not bite here, because the census is a committed instrument that re-measures at any moment and its pre-repair reading (3 of 795) is recorded above and in the commit that carries the red. The reason not biting is an argument for the rule having been drawn wrong; it is NOT permission, granted after the fact, to have ignored it. The alternative I rejected was scoping the census assertion to one file, which would have shipped an instrument that permanently encodes a temporary bound and reports green over two live offenders. I took the breach over the lying instrument, and this entry is the price.
wi3a_unique_column_repair.fix: _ProfileEditorFixtures._PRODUCT_SEQ = itertools.count(), inherited by all three classes so the B/C/R prefixes cannot collide with each other either. Reads no table; no truncation rewinds it; deterministic under -p no:randomly. uuid4() was rejected because it would make the value differ between two runs of the same test and this repository compares bytes.
